title: Solar geoengineering governance framework
bottleneck: Solar radiation modification could cool the planet but no legitimate global governance exists to decide whether, when, or how it is researched or deployed: the CBD has a de-facto moratorium on outdoor experiments, UNEA talks collapsed without consensus, and in 2025 all 54 African states backed a non-use agreement while a startup got $60M for SRM experiments. Unilateral deployment by one actor would affect every nation's climate, yet there is no forum with authority to stop it.
why_it_blocks: The governance vacuum is itself dangerous: it invites rogue experimentation while blocking the coordinated research needed to understand risks. Either ungoverned deployment or a panicked ban could produce worse outcomes than careful, governed inquiry.
current_state: The EU Parliament calls for an EU moratorium and global framework, the UK launched a 56.8M pound research program in 2025, and the EU's chief scientific advisors issued a formal opinion in 2024. But no path to binding international governance has emerged.
